description: This topic explains the reproductive systems of farm animals, the oestrus cycle, mating and fertilisation, gestation and parturition, methods of mating including artificial insemination, and the systems and objectives of animal breeding and selection.

mcq.questionText: Which organ in the female reproductive system of a cow is the site where the foetus develops during pregnancy?
mcq.explanation: The uterus (womb) is the organ where the fertilised egg implants and the foetus grows until birth.

mcq.questionText: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilisation usually take place?
mcq.explanation: Fertilisation, the union of sperm and ovum, normally occurs in the oviduct (Fallopian tube).

mcq.questionText: Which organ produces the male reproductive cells (sperms) and the hormone testosterone in a bull?
mcq.explanation: The testes produce sperms and secrete the male hormone testosterone, which controls male characteristics.

mcq.questionText: The period during which a female animal is on heat and ready to accept the male for mating is called the:
mcq.explanation: Oestrus, commonly called 'heat', is the time when a female is sexually receptive and ready to mate.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common sign of heat (oestrus) in a dairy cow?

options.text: Loss of appetite for several days
Standing still to be mounted by other cows
Shedding of hair on the back

mcq.explanation: A clear sign of heat is the 'standing heat', where the cow stands still and allows other cows to mount her; she may also be restless, bellow and produce clear mucus.

mcq.questionText: The length of time from successful mating (fertilisation) to the birth of the young one is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The gestation period is the duration of pregnancy, from fertilisation until parturition (birth).

mcq.questionText: Approximately how long is the gestation period of cattle?
mcq.explanation: Cattle have a gestation period of about nine months (around 280 to 285 days).

mcq.questionText: The act of giving birth in farm animals is technically called:
mcq.explanation: Parturition is the process of giving birth; in cattle it is also called calving, in pigs farrowing, and in goats and sheep kidding and lambing.

mcq.questionText: Which method of mating involves placing semen into the female's reproductive tract using special equipment instead of a natural male?
mcq.explanation: Artificial insemination (A.I.) is the introduction of collected semen into the female reproductive tract by a technician using an insemination gun, without a bull.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of artificial insemination (A.I.) over natural mating?

options.text: It helps to control the spread of breeding diseases
It works even without keeping records
It needs no special storage of semen

mcq.explanation: A.I. reduces the spread of diseases transmitted during mating and allows one superior bull to serve many cows over a wide area.

mcq.questionText: The mating of closely related animals, such as a bull with its own daughters, is called:
mcq.explanation: Inbreeding is the mating of closely related animals; it fixes desirable traits but may concentrate undesirable genes if overdone.

mcq.questionText: Mating animals of two different breeds, for example a local Tanzanian Shorthorn Zebu cow with a Friesian bull, is known as:
mcq.explanation: Crossbreeding mates animals of different breeds to combine good qualities of both and produce vigorous offspring (hybrid vigour).

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major objective of animal breeding?

options.text: To reduce the number of useful animals
To improve production and disease resistance
To make all animals look identical for shows
To increase the cost of keeping animals

mcq.explanation: Animal breeding aims to improve productivity (milk, meat, eggs), disease resistance, growth rate and product quality.

mcq.questionText: Continually mating local cows with pure-bred exotic bulls over several generations to gradually improve the local stock is called:
mcq.explanation: Upgrading (grading up) means mating low-grade local females with pure-bred males repeatedly so that the offspring increasingly resemble the improved breed.

mcq.questionText: When choosing a cow for breeding for milk, which characteristic is most desirable?

options.text: High milk yield and good body conformation

mcq.explanation: Breeding stock should be selected for high productivity (such as high milk yield), good conformation, fertility, health and disease resistance.

fib.questionText: The female reproductive cell produced by the ovary is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The ovary produces the ovum (egg), the female gamete that is fertilised by a sperm.

fib.questionText: The release of a mature egg from the ovary is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Ovulation is the release of a ripe ovum from the ovary, usually around the time of heat.

fib.questionText: The time when a female animal is ready and willing to mate is called the period of _____.
fib.explanation: Oestrus, or heat, is the receptive period within the oestrus cycle when the female accepts the male.

fib.questionText: The union of a sperm and an ovum to form a zygote is called _____.
fib.explanation: Fertilisation is the fusion of the male and female gametes to begin a new individual.

fib.questionText: The gestation period of goats and sheep is about _____ months.
fib.explanation: Goats and sheep carry their young for approximately five months (about 150 days).

fib.questionText: The gestation period of a pig is roughly 3 months, 3 weeks and 3 _____.
fib.explanation: A pig's gestation is commonly remembered as 3 months, 3 weeks and 3 days (about 114 days).

fib.questionText: Introducing semen into a female's reproductive tract using equipment instead of a male animal is called _____ insemination.
fib.explanation: Artificial insemination (A.I.) places collected semen into the female tract without natural service.

fib.questionText: Mating animals that are not related at all, to introduce new blood, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Outbreeding (outcrossing) is mating unrelated animals of the same breed to add vigour and reduce inbreeding effects.

fib.questionText: Choosing the best animals with desirable qualities to be parents of the next generation is called _____.
fib.explanation: Selection is picking superior animals as breeding stock so that good traits are passed on.

fib.questionText: The act of giving birth in a cow is specifically called _____.
fib.explanation: Parturition in cattle is called calving; in pigs it is farrowing and in sheep it is lambing.

tf.questionText: The testes of a bull are held outside the body in the scrotum to keep them cooler for sperm production.
tf.explanation: The scrotum keeps the testes slightly cooler than body temperature, which is necessary for healthy sperm production.

tf.questionText: Fertilisation in farm animals normally takes place in the vagina.
tf.explanation: Fertilisation normally occurs in the oviduct (Fallopian tube), not in the vagina.

tf.questionText: A cow that is on heat may become restless, bellow more, and allow other cows to mount her.
tf.explanation: These are typical signs of oestrus in cattle and help the farmer know the right time to serve the cow.

tf.questionText: The gestation period of cattle is about three months.
tf.explanation: Cattle have a gestation of about nine months; pigs are the ones with about three months and three weeks.

tf.questionText: Artificial insemination allows semen from one outstanding bull to be used to serve many cows.
tf.explanation: One superior bull's semen can be collected, stored and used on many cows, spreading its good genes widely.

tf.questionText: A disadvantage of artificial insemination is that it requires trained technicians and proper storage of semen.
tf.explanation: A.I. needs skilled personnel, correct heat detection and facilities (such as liquid nitrogen) to store semen, which can be costly.

tf.questionText: Inbreeding done continuously for many generations can lead to weaker offspring and more inherited defects.
tf.explanation: Excessive inbreeding concentrates harmful recessive genes, causing reduced fertility, slow growth and inherited weaknesses.

tf.questionText: Crossbreeding a local Zebu cow with a Friesian bull can produce offspring that give more milk than the local breed.
tf.explanation: Crossbreeding combines the high milk yield of the Friesian with the hardiness of the Zebu, often raising milk production.

tf.questionText: Upgrading means mating two completely different species, such as a cow and a goat.
tf.explanation: Upgrading is repeatedly mating local females with pure-bred males of the same species to improve the stock, not crossing different species.

tf.questionText: A pregnant cow should be given good feed and gentle handling, and should be separated from rough or aggressive animals.
tf.explanation: Proper care of a pregnant animal includes adequate nutrition, clean water, gentle handling and protection from stress to avoid abortion.

summary.questionText: Name the main parts of the female reproductive system of a cow.
summary.correctAnswer: The ovaries, oviducts (Fallopian tubes), uterus (womb), cervix, vagina and vulva.
summary.explanation: These parts work together to produce eggs, allow fertilisation, carry the foetus and deliver the young one.

summary.questionText: Name the main parts of the male reproductive system of a bull.
summary.correctAnswer: The testes, scrotum, epididymis, vas deferens, accessory glands and penis.
summary.explanation: These produce, store and deliver sperm during mating.

summary.questionText: State three signs of heat (oestrus) in a dairy cow.
summary.correctAnswer: Standing to be mounted, restlessness and frequent bellowing, swollen vulva with clear mucus, and reduced milk yield.
summary.explanation: Recognising these signs helps the farmer serve the cow at the right time for conception.

summary.questionText: Give the approximate gestation periods of cattle, goats/sheep and pigs.
summary.correctAnswer: Cattle about 9 months, goats and sheep about 5 months, and pigs about 3 months 3 weeks 3 days.
summary.explanation: Knowing gestation periods helps farmers plan feeding, housing and the expected date of birth.

summary.correctAnswer: Artificial insemination is the placing of collected semen into the female reproductive tract using equipment instead of allowing natural mating.
summary.explanation: A.I. lets farmers use semen from superior males to improve their herds.

summary.questionText: State two advantages and two disadvantages of artificial insemination.
summary.correctAnswer: Advantages: controls breeding diseases and lets one superior bull serve many cows. Disadvantages: needs skilled technicians and special storage of semen, and requires accurate heat detection.
summary.explanation: A.I. improves genetics and disease control but depends on skill and facilities.

summary.questionText: What is meant by animal breeding?
summary.correctAnswer: Animal breeding is the selecting and mating of animals to produce offspring with improved or desired qualities.
summary.explanation: Its purpose is to improve production, growth, quality and disease resistance.

summary.correctAnswer: Inbreeding, line breeding, outbreeding (outcrossing), crossbreeding and upgrading.
summary.explanation: Each method differs in how closely related or different the mated animals are.

summary.questionText: List three desirable characteristics to look for when selecting breeding stock.
summary.correctAnswer: High productivity (milk, meat or eggs), good fertility, disease resistance, good body conformation and fast growth.
summary.explanation: Choosing animals with these traits ensures better offspring.

summary.questionText: State three ways of caring for a pregnant farm animal.
summary.correctAnswer: Provide adequate balanced feed and clean water, handle the animal gently and avoid stress, protect it from disease, and prepare a clean place for birth.
summary.explanation: Good care reduces the risk of abortion and ensures a healthy mother and young one.

hoq.questionText: A farmer in Tanga keeps local Zebu cows that give little milk. He wants to greatly increase milk yield over several generations while keeping the animals adapted to the hot climate. Which breeding strategy is most suitable?

options.text: Continuous close inbreeding of his Zebu cows
Upgrading by serving the Zebu cows with pure Friesian semen through A.I. over several generations
Selling all cows and buying goats
Mating the cows with bulls of a different species

hoq.explanation: Upgrading the local Zebu with a high-yielding dairy breed such as Friesian through A.I. gradually raises milk production while crossbred offspring retain some Zebu hardiness; inbreeding would not improve yield.

hoq.questionText: A dairy farmer notices his cow standing to be mounted at 7:00 a.m. and wants the best chance of conception using A.I. What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Wait one full week before calling the A.I. technician
Inseminate the cow within about 12 hours, later the same day
Inseminate the cow immediately the next month
Ignore it because standing heat is not a fertile sign

hoq.explanation: Standing heat indicates the fertile period; insemination is most successful when done within about 12 hours after the cow first stands to be mounted, matching ovulation timing.

hoq.questionText: A breeder repeatedly mates a champion ram only with its own daughters for many years and notices the lambs are becoming smaller and less fertile. What is the most likely cause and the best correction?

options.text: Too much crossbreeding; he should inbreed more
Inbreeding depression; he should introduce an unrelated ram (outbreeding)
Good upgrading; he should continue unchanged
Poor feeding only; breeding has no effect

hoq.explanation: Continuous close inbreeding causes inbreeding depression, with reduced size and fertility from concentrated harmful genes; introducing an unrelated ram (outbreeding) brings new blood and restores vigour.
